Need use criterion: violation when vague, underspecified, overloaded, unclear terms allow materially different requirements interpretations; do not flag harmless stylistic variation. We need output only JSON object. Need decide for each. Let's reason story by story.

We need understand Unambiguous criterion scope individual. We need identify terms/phrases that lead to materially different interpretations. Many user stories have vague terms. Need decide.

BC-001: "As a anonymoususer, I want to view a list of sponsors, so that I can thank all the awesome sponsors." Seems clear enough? "list of sponsors" clear. "view" maybe clear. No ambiguous. No Violation.

BC-002: "view a list of user profiles, so that I know who is attending conference." clear? Maybe "user profiles" clear. Not ambiguous. No violation.

BC-003: As trainingcoordinator, want to email all trainers at once from website for info and updates, so that It is easier to use. "email all trainers at once from website" maybe clear. No materially ambiguous? Maybe not.

BC-004: "very clear map where buildings and rooms are" - "very clear map" is subjective but not materially different requirements? Maybe vague "very clear" but not ambiguous? Need decide. "very clear map" could mean detailed map with buildings and rooms, acceptable. "where buildings and rooms are" clear. Could be no violation? Possibly "very clear" is vague but not material? Hmm.

BC-005: "As a trainer, I want to edit my training node myself, so that the training coordinators don't have to and links to slides." This is poorly formed: "and links to slides" appended. Ambiguous: "links to slides" maybe want add links to slides? The story says "edit my training node myself, so that ... and links to slides" - unclear whether requirement includes adding links to slides. Violation.

BC-006: As a trainee, want to limit to one registration per day per authenticated user, so that we don't have duplicate spaces. Role "trainee" but requirement is system limiting? "limit to one registration per day per authenticated user" is clear. "duplicate spaces" maybe clear. No violation maybe.

BC-007: "admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee so that, so that we can see if attendend, refunded, no show." Typo "attendend" maybe status values unclear? "attendend, refunded, no show" clear statuses though misspelled. The phrase "helps track registration status" could be vague? But status listed. I think no violation? Though "so that, so that" duplicate not ambiguity. Maybe "attendend" typo creates unclear? Probably not materially, still attended. No violation.

BC-008: "As a attendee, I want to be added to a training waitlist, so that so they can be considered for a class." Pronoun "they" mismatched, but meaning clear. No ambiguous? Wait "added to a training waitlist" no specific training? Could be ambiguous: which training? But context maybe add to waitlist for full training. Material? Could be unspecified but not multiple interpretations? Maybe violation? "a training waitlist" could mean any training; but as user story, need select training. However individual criterion: "a training waitlist" may be underspecified but likely no materially different interpretations if waitlist is for selected class. Maybe not flag.

BC-009: "As a trainee, I want to must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox, so that they can be accountable.." Clear enough: must accept cancellation terms with checkbox. "cancellation terms" maybe specific enough? Terms defined elsewhere? Could be ambiguous? Probably no.

BC-010: "As a trainingcoordinator, I want to tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists, so that so we don't loose money or spots." "whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists" is vague/underspecified and uncertain: what workflow? Ambiguous. Violation likely.

BC-011: "As a trainee, I want to add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site, so that they can schedule their event experience." Conditional "if there is a schedule feature on the site" makes requirement ambiguous: if no feature? Maybe not clear. "add to my schedule" unclear what action. Violation.

BC-012: "As a trainee, I want to see which trainings I have signed up for, so that they can schedule their event experience." Clear. No violation.

The URL path should be SEO friendly /training/training-title, so that I can choose the right class, AND the trainer can tweet and promote their class." This is detailed; "possibly a map view" is ambiguous? It says maybe map, so optional but uncertain requirement. "SEO friendly /training/training-title" clear. Could be no violation? Yet "possibly a map view" introduces optionality, ambiguous whether required. But main page info listed. Is that materially different? A map view might be optional.
